title: AI Agent for Brand Mentions and Replies: 2026 Guide
summary: An ai agent for brand mentions and replies works best matched to your approval needs. Choose dedicated tools, workflow platforms, or autonomous responses.
body_markdown:
## Where Activepieces fits for mention and reply workflows


A reply agent is not code to be run; it is a user posting under your brand, and a library gives it no tenant, no role and no audit log.


Activepieces treats it that way: admins control which apps a team may connect, credentials are held centrally, and the agent gets least privilege of its own, with custom RBAC, SSO and SCIM provisioning around it.


> A reply agent is not code to be run; it is a user posting under your brand, and a library gives it no tenant, no role and no audit log.


In the run detail view each tool call is listed separately with its own input and output, so a bad reply traces back to the exact drafting call instead of one opaque result. Moneypenny and MoneyGram run it in production.


That follows from the last point. If your rule fits a workflow builder, you don't need engineers to enforce it.


### What it can do for this job


Start with the trigger the screenshot below shows, the one that matters here: "Catch Webhook." Your social listening tool sends each mention to that URL. The next step can draft a reply with an AI model, using whatever key you supply.


Before anything posts, a flow can then pause for a person to approve, and the run history records what went in and what came out.


In the screenshot, the Version History panel shows two saved versions of one flow. Each has a timestamp and a status dot, with a "Push to Git" option in the menu beside it.


For a reply workflow, that means you can see which version of the drafting logic was live when a given answer went out, and roll back if a prompt change produced worse replies.


### What it does not do


It doesn't find mentions. Without a listening tool feeding the webhook, the flow never starts.


It also has no inbox, no sentiment view and no thread context of its own, so a reviewer sees what you map into the approval step and nothing more. Map too little and they approve blind.


I couldn't confirm from its own pages whether every social network you care about has a ready-made posting step. Check the specific network and action before you commit. A long catalogue count tells you little; the one action your reply needs is what decides it.


### Cost and hosting from its pricing page


If self-hosting matters,[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) has an MIT-licensed core that you can run on your own servers as the free Community Edition, and its free cloud plan includes unlimited flows with 1,000 credits a month. n8n is the It also has self-hosting.


Read the current pricing page for task caps, and for whether approval steps and Git versioning sit on the plan you would use.


For this job, the ranking splits in two: Activepieces and n8n suit teams that want self-hosting, and Activepieces allows unlimited flows on every plan, free included. Zapier and Make suit teams that would rather not run anything themselves.
